title: Samsung has delayed its Android 17 update
snippet: Samsung appears to be delaying the rollout of its Android 17 update, at least slightly, with pushback in some regions. more…
fullText:
Samsung appears to be delaying the rollout of its Android 17 update, at least slightly, with pushback in some regions.

The launch of a stable One UI 9 rollout for Galaxy S26 was first announced last week, with the Android 17-based update landing first on Samsung’s current flagship before expanding to more devices. Samsung explicitly said the rollout was supposed to start on September 16, but it doesn’t appear to have shown up for anyone just yet. 

While the reason is unclear, SammyGuru spotted a sort of confirmation that Samsung has delayed its Android 17 in some capacity.

A press release around the One UI 9 rollout on Samsung’s Newsroom in Thailand noted a rollout date of September 21 originally, but was updated to say September 28, and now appears to have been updated again to remove a specific date altogether, only saying “September 2026” at this point.

	

This isn’t unprecedented; Samsung has had numerous major updates be delayed quietly at the last moment, but it’s certainly not the best start for One UI 9’s rollout. Hopefully, whatever issues are pushing Samsung’s schedule back can be fixed as soon as possible.

title: Adobe Premiere for Android launches for free with layered video editing, YouTube templates
snippet: Months after it arrived on iPhone, Adobe Premiere’s mobile version is now available on Android devices with layered video editing, templates, foldable optimization, and more. more…
fullText:
Months after it arrived on iPhone, Adobe Premiere’s mobile version is now available on Android devices with layered video editing, templates, foldable optimization, and more.

Adobe Premiere Pro is widely recognized as a powerful video editing suite on desktop machines, but Adobe’s last version for mobile devices vanished a while back. Now, Adobe Premiere is once again available on Android, delivering what appears to be a very capable video editor that promises to be a solution across all Android devices.

This is the same app that debuted on iPhone in late 2025, and it brings quite a few features with it.

Some of the key features include:

	

Enhance Audio: Reduce background noise, clean up voiceovers, etc

Multi-track timeline: Manage multiple videos, sound effects, music, etc

Templates: Custom-made templates to speed up editing

Effects: Transitions, creative assets, Adobe Stock integration

Export: Up to 4K editing + export

The app already has wide support of different Android devices and form factors, including optimization for foldable smartphones. There’s also a built-in voice recorder.

Adobe says that more features are coming, including support for Adobe Fonts in creating text overlays, the ability to transfer projects to Premiere Pro on desktop, “beat detection,” cropping, and more. 

The big deal here, though, is that Adobe Premiere for Android is free. You don’t need a Creative Cloud subscription, you don’t need to sit through ads, and there are no watermarks either. Adobe says you can purchase upgrades for “additional generative credits and storage,” but that’s optional.

Requirements for Adobe Premiere on Android include 5GB of RAM or more and Android 13 or newer.

Apple updated TestFlight this week with support for landscape orientation, and for macOS 27 Golden Gate’s new resizable iPhone Mirroring window. Here are the details.

TestFlight now supports landscape orientation on iOS

title: Pixel 11 starts testing ‘Call for Me’ to have Gemini phone on your behalf
snippet: Following Direct My Call and Hold for Me, Google is introducing “Call for Me” on the Pixel 11 series. more…
fullText:
Following Direct My Call and Hold for Me, Google is introducing “Call for Me” on the Pixel 11 series.

Reminiscent of Google Duplex, this Gemini Intelligence feature is officially an “early experiment” to let Google handle “routine phone calls” to book appointments, place items on hold, and reschedule reservations. Examples include 

reserve patio seating at a restaurant

check if a hardware store has a specific part in stock

move your haircut appointment to next Thursday

Google says it will “respect the time of the neighborhood shops and front-desk staff answering the phone,” and that “calls made by Gemini on behalf of the user represent real customers conducting real transactions.”

Asking AI to speak on your behalf is a big step that requires genuine trust. That’s why we built this experience around user control.

Your Pixel 11 will “call on your behalf using the Gemini app.” Users see a live transcript and can take over at any point.  Gemini will “introduce itself” and “handle the conversation with the person on the other end.” As part of this, it can wait on hold and navigate any automated phone menus.

	

Google is “starting small to get the experience right.” As of today, an early preview is rolling out to Gemini subscribers using the enrolled in the Phone by Google beta on the Pixel 11, 11 Pro, 11 Pro XL, and 11 Pro Fold in the US. More details are available here.

title: Android’s Digital Wellbeing appears to be ditching ‘Heads up’ walking alerts
snippet: Google appears to be pulling the plug on a Digital Wellbeing feature called “Heads up” which is designed to help you stay off of your phone for extended periods of time while walking. more…
fullText:
Google appears to be pulling the plug on a Digital Wellbeing feature called “Heads up” which is designed to help you stay off of your phone for extended periods of time while walking.

Introduced in 2021, “Heads up” was designed to help you curb your smartphone use while walking since, when looking at your phone, you’re probably not fully aware of your surroundings. Alerts such as “Look ahead” and “Watch your step” would appear if you were using your phone while walking for a certain length of time.

Now, Google seems to be removing it.

In the Digital Wellbeing v1.48.975819457.beta release, the folks over at Android Authority noticed strings regarding “Heads up deprecation.” Google explicitly says:

	

Walking detection is going away soon

There’s no word on why it’s being removed, though it’s certainly odd given that the feature at least appears to run on device. It’s easy to guess that the feature was probably underused, being an opt-in feature, but it’s strange seeing as there’s no obvious burden to just leaving it in place. 

As it stands, the feature is still active and, with the altered strings only in the beta track, it’s probably not going away imminently, but we’ll have to wait and see what other details come to light as the removal nears.

title: Tim Cook meets EU chief Ursula von der Leyen as bloc pushes new child safety rules
snippet: Keeping with Apple’s pledge that Tim Cook would remain involved in Apple’s government relations around the world after stepping down as CEO, he met this week with Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Keeping with Apple’s pledge that Tim Cook would remain involved in Apple’s government relations around the world after stepping down as CEO, he met this week with Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission. Here are the details.

Tim Cook discusses EU Kids Act with EC President

When Apple announced that Tim Cook would step down as CEO on September 1, the company said:

As executive chairman, Cook will assist with certain aspects of the company, including engaging with policymakers around the world.

Since taking up the job of executive chairman, Cook has kept with this promise.

Just days ago, Bloomberg reported that Cook would attend a White House state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping, which is scheduled for Thursday evening, September 24.

The report came just a few days before Cook posted on X that he had welcomed Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese at Apple Park.

It was great to welcome @AlboMP to Apple Park this morning to talk about the incredible work of our teams and our longstanding commitment to Australia. I was grateful to share some of our newest innovations, including strong and intuitive controls to help keep kids safe online. pic.twitter.com/EQKmIkP3uC

— Tim Cook (@tim_cook) September 19, 2026

After the meeting, Albanese reportedly shared that Cook described Australia’s social media restrictions for children as “world-leading.”

Yesterday, Cook continued his string of encounters with world leaders, sitting down with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen.

In a post on X, von der Leyen said the two discussed the EU Kids Act and “agreed on the importance of privacy, safety and security for children.”

Good discussion with @tim_cook in the margins of UNGA.

 We discussed the EU Kids Act, and agreed on the importance of privacy, safety and security for children.

Tech companies innovate and bring huge benefits to our society.

They must do so in a way that empowers parents and… pic.twitter.com/Ygv2x8893X

— Ursula von der Leyen (@vonderleyen) September 21, 2026

This proposed legislation is set to restrict social media access for minors across the EU and require platforms to provide stronger protections for young users.

The meeting happened in Manhattan, where world leaders are currently gathering for the United Nations General Assembly.

It is currently unclear whether Cook will meet or has already met with other world leaders, but if he has, there is a good chance we’ll hear about it from the officials themselves sooner rather than later.

title: Microsoft’s New Surface Laptops Embody the PC-Phone Marriage Snapdragon Promised Years Ago
snippet: Qualcomm’s PC chips were developed with the company’s phone DNA. Two generations in, we’re seeing payoffs.
fullText:
On the stage for the second day of keynotes at Snapdragon Summit 2026, Microsoft Corporate VP of Surface Devices Brett Ostrum revealed new versions of the company’s 12-inch Surface Pro and 13-inch Surface laptops, both of which now run Qualcomm’s Snapdragon Elite X2 chips for improved performance and battery life. These chips had come to larger Surface devices earlier in the year, and arrived in the smaller sizes of Microsoft’s portable PC lineup.

Along with the chip upgrade, both of the updated Surface devices have increased RAM options of 16GB and 24GB (up from 8GB and 16GB in their predecessors).

But some hidden advantages of running Qualcomm’s Snapdragon Elite X2, which was introduced at last year’s Snapdragon Summit, are downstream of the years the company spent developing smartphone silicon. 

			

More from CNET

The first Snapdragon X Elite chips were revealed in 2023 as Qualcomm’s big return to PC silicon, attempting to outdo Apple laptops in battery life and performance. A big part of the company’s pitch was using what it learned making phone chips to see benefits in the laptop space. Now, we’re seeing evidence of that DNA paying off.

For instance, Ostrum told me after the keynote that the new Surface devices have superior cameras to their rivals thanks to the image signal processing on the Elite X2 chips, inherited from phone camera hardware, that will make you look amazing on Zoom calls.

The 13-inch Surface Laptop and 12-inch Surface Pro received Snapdragon X2 upgrades, and the new Surface Mouse has haptics to buzz and pulse your palm.Katie Collins/CNET

Before, Apple had taken the crown of image quality in its laptop webcams, Ostrum said. But thanks to Qualcomm’s investment in ISP and the camera pipeline, the Surface devices have seen a big turnaround in the video quality captured by their webcams. 

“With our [Surface] Pro and laptops that we announced earlier this year [with] Snapdragon X2 Elite, we took the No. 1 and No. 2 spots from Apple in terms of camera quality,” Ostrum said, referring to DxOMark’s laptop rankings. Those rankings currently place Microsoft’s 13.8-inch Surface Laptop and 13-inch Surface Pro in first and second place, above Apple’s MacBook Pro models, in camera quality.

It’s not the first thing consumers or commercial buyers look at when shopping for laptops and two-in-ones, but people now spend so much time in Teams and Zoom meetings that camera quality is more important than consumers might admit. And considering how much the bar has been raised by ever-improving phone cameras, it’s no surprise that people want and expect an improved webcam.

“You want to look good when you show up [on camera], and it’s important to us, it’s important to our customers. And so it’s a fairly straightforward approach for us to say we want to make this look as good as we can,” Ostrum said.

We’re not just talking about better camera hardware, either. Ostrum was quick to say that it isn’t the lenses or sensors that make the difference — it’s the image processing pipeline Qualcomm has refined.

“I can put the same sensors into multiple silicon platforms, but the best solution is going to come with a Qualcomm ISP,” Ostrum said. “If you compare an Intel-based one of our commercial devices to a Qualcomm-based solution, you will see the difference.”

Both the new 12-inch Surface Pro (left) and 13-inch Surface Laptop (right) pack Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X2 Elite chips.David Lumb/CNET

Phone chip DNA doesn’t just help with cameras — it boosts battery, too

That’s not the end of smartphones’ influence on laptops. The older x86 chips may have been adapted to laptops, but they originated in a world where PCs plugged into walls, Ostrum said, implying that they struggled with battery life. But the Snapdragon phone chip DNA and its emphasis on performance per watt have noticeably extended the battery life on Surface devices while also delivering the fast speeds consumers need for their tasks. 

“People raved about the first generation of devices from a performance perspective, but the thing that we heard unanimously that was just a huge delight was, ‘The battery life’s incredible. The battery life’s incredible. The battery life’s incredible,'” Ostrum said. 

There’s more that goes into the battery life of the Surface Pro and Surface laptop than the chip, including redesigning the interior for better thermal management. Roughly speaking, better heat management means more time running at high performance and less energy spent cooling the device down, which means more battery life. It’s all connected.

“We oftentimes will see as much gen-over-gen performance improvement from the thermal design that we iterate on as we do from the chip improvement gen-over-gen,” Ostrum said. 

Still, that’s combining what Microsoft does best with the advantages of Qualcomm silicon, at least as far as Ostrum sees it. Microsoft expects 22.5 hours of battery life from the second-gen 13-inch Surface laptop, which is slightly down from the 24 hours offered by its predecessor. We’ll see how those expectations bear out in our testing. 

What is true is how much longer those expectations are than what they were before Microsoft switched to Qualcomm — the Surface Laptop 5 and 6 with Intel-based chips had 18.5 hours of expected battery life, though the internet is strewn with reports of units only lasting half that time, or even less. Switching to a chip that inherited priorities and design architecture from mobile silicon seems to have helped.

Editors’ note: David Lumb’s travel costs were covered by Qualcomm. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

snippet: The Android Dev Summit is returning in 2026 after Google’s last focused developer conference in 2022. Additionally, the agenda comes with a mention of Android 18. more…
fullText:
The Android Dev Summit is returning in 2026 after Google’s last focused developer conference in 2022. Additionally, the agenda comes with a mention of Android 18.

The last Android Dev Summit was in 2022. The developer-focused event is now back with two days of programming at Google’s headquarters in Mountain View, as well as a satellite “Extended” event in London.

There will be a “keynote with Android leadership on the latest features and updates.” There are four conference tracks: AI experiences, Android XR, Apps foundation, and Tools and performance. 

Meanwhile, we get our first mention of Android 18, including how there will be “powerful new graphics features.”

	

“Elevate your apps with the latest graphics features in Jetpack Compose and Android 18” is a particularly interesting session:

Ready to take your Android UI from “it works” to “it’s a work of art”? 

Join us for a tour of the latest graphics capabilities in Jetpack Compose. We’ll show you how to build new visual effects, from delightful mesh gradients to progressive blurs, and using the powerful new graphics features in Android 18. We will also show you how to improve the performance of your graphics features, without sacrificing battery life or frame rates.

It will be interesting to see if Android 18 is announced at or just before the conference. Android no longer has developer previews in light of the Canary channel. But for reference, Android 16 testing began in November. Any sort of Android 18 preview in October would be very early.

Android XR and AI are big focuses, with notable sessions about how to:

Connect your apps to Gemini, Search and the Android intelligence system: “Explore how to connect your applications seamlessly to Gemini, Search and the Android intelligence system.”

title: Brazil court tells Apple to add age checks for casino app purchases
snippet: A Brazilian court has ordered Apple to tighten age controls around a casino-style app on the App Store, including requiring age verification before making in-app purchases. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
A Brazilian court has ordered Apple to tighten age controls around a casino-style app on the App Store, including requiring age verification before making in-app purchases. Here are the details.

Apple ordered to strengthen App Store age checks in Brazil

As reported by Tilt, São Paulo’s Court of Justice has granted an emergency injunction requiring Apple to restrict minors’ access to the “Casino Roulette: Roulettist” app.

The decision came after four child and adolescent rights groups filed a civil lawsuit in July, alleging that minors were able to download casino-style games from the App Store and purchase virtual chips with real money, despite Casino Roulette: Roulettist carrying an 18+ age rating.

In the decision, the court gave Apple five days to block new downloads of Casino Roulette: Roulettist by users registered as minors, and require “age verification for purchases of virtual chips with real money to continue playing or expand the in-app experience,” says Tilt.

Beyond the specific app, the decision also bars Apple from allowing new apps with equivalent casino-style mechanics onto the App Store without effective age controls.

Tilt says the court also told Apple to preserve all records related to the app and present a technical report detailing the measures it has taken. The court also established a daily fine of R$100,000 (roughly $19,500) for noncompliance.

Tilt reached out to Apple for comment, but the company had not responded at the time of publication.

title: iPhone 18 Pro one week later: Zero compromises
snippet: I’ve been using iPhone 18 Pro for the past week after a full year as an iPhone Air user. And while there are advantages with each model, my main takeaway about iPhone 18 Pro so far is that it has zero compromises. Here’s what I mean. more…
fullText:
I’ve been using iPhone 18 Pro for the past week after a full year as an iPhone Air user. And while there are advantages with each model, my main takeaway about iPhone 18 Pro so far is that it has zero compromises. Here’s what I mean.

iPhone 18 Pro: The best camera system, battery life, and performance

If you want to buy a new iPhone, chances are the iPhone 18 Pro is a strong contender.

I’ve had mine for a week now, a Burgundy model that replaced my iPhone Air. And despite loving the Air a lot, it’s hard to match Apple’s no-compromise approach to the iPhone 18 Pro.

Cameras are better and far more versatile on iPhone 18 Pro compared to the Air. Telephoto and Ultra Wide lenses are great for specific use cases, but even the Main camera is better on iPhone 18 Pro.

Battery life is similarly impressive. I generally found the iPhone Air’s battery good enough for everyday use, and only needed to charge mid-day occasionally. But with iPhone 18 Pro I don’t even have to think about battery.

Performance is fantastic too. The A20 Pro chip makes everything on the iPhone feel fast, and I’ve even noticed a more responsive Siri AI. Thanks to the vapor chamber, I haven’t had any issues of overheating either, which the Air sometimes struggled with.

I’m not a pro photographer, and if you want battery tests or performance benchmarks, my colleague Chance’s iPhone 18 Pro review has you covered. But after a week with iPhone 18 Pro, that word “best” keeps coming back to me.

iPhone 18 Pro (and Pro Max) pack the absolute best camera system Apple makes, have the best battery life, and perform better than any other models. I’ve even noticed smaller improvements: the better built-in speakers and Dynamic Island upgrades are highlights.

There are measurable differences in all these areas, but I also appreciate just knowing my iPhone has the “best” Apple offers in key areas that matter most. There’s no wondering: would these pictures of my family look better if I used a different iPhone? Would this slowdown have happened?

All the positives of iPhone 18 Pro aside though, I’ll admit that I’m still very intrigued by the forthcoming iPhone Duo.

iPhone Duo, like iPhone Air, will be compromised but so compelling

The iPhone Air and iPhone Duo share a lot in common. Besides having similar design traits, they also both have shortcomings.

Like my iPhone Air, the iPhone Duo will have a worse camera system than iPhone 18 Pro. Battery might be comparable but definitely worse than the Pro Max, and I suspect sustained performance will lag a bit too. iPhone Duo will also lack Face ID and the Action button.

Yet despite these compromises, I’m very excited to get my hands on the device. 

That’s because it offers a lot of compelling innovations not found in iPhone 18 Pro. The foldable form factor represents arguably the biggest iPhone hardware change ever.

I’ve been enjoying my iPhone 18 Pro a lot. But guess what happened when I picked up the iPhone Air the other day?

I instantly said, “Wow.”

Here’s my iPhone 18 Pro Max review:

Do not buy an iPhone Air unless you want to immediately return every other phone forever.

— Ben Thompson (@benthompson) September 21, 2026

title: Google says Gemini 4 release is coming ‘as soon as possible’
snippet: As its rivals continue to iterate quickly, Google has confirmed that its Gemini 4 flagship AI model is nearing release and that it is coming “as soon as possible.” more…
fullText:
As its rivals continue to iterate quickly, Google has confirmed that its Gemini 4 flagship AI model is nearing release and that it is coming “as soon as possible.”

Google DeepMind chief Koray Kavukcuoglu confirmed to The Information at the publication’s AI Agenda Live Summit this week that its next flagship Gemini model, Gemini 4, has entered “post-training,” a phase in which the model’s behavior is refined ahead of a public release. This includes safety testing and implementing guardrails, with internal testing underway using Gemini 4 to power Antigravity.

In other words, Google is getting closer to the release of Gemini 4.

Kavukcuoglu explained:

	

Our intention is to, like—as soon as possible—to release an early post-training output because we see the results and we are excited… [to] continue the fast-paced iterations.

He adds that he hopes the model will be released “much earlier” than the end of 2026, but a specific timeline was not shared.

The update comes just days after Anthropic and OpenAI have both launched major updates to their respective flagship AI models in recent weeks. Responding to the idea that Google has “fallen behind,” Kavukcuoglu said that “I have the utmost trust in the team” and that “in my mind, it’s a certainty that we are always gonna be at the frontier.”

Google’s last major flagship model release was in November 2025 with Gemini 3 Pro, followed by Gemini 3.1 Pro in February 2026. There have been several updates to Flash and other models in the time since, most recently with Gemini 3.8 Flash. Google teased Gemini 3.5 Pro over the Summer, but never ended up releasing the model, and this week’s conversation with The Information sheds no light on whether or not that model will be released – Kavukcuoglu said that Google “took a little bit of a step back” to focus on its Flash models instead, but that the current focus is on releasing Gemini 4.

Speaking on AGI, a common conversation around other major AI model updates, Kavukcuoglu says that “the conversation is more about are we able to build intelligent agents that we can trust.”

title: Online CVS Shoppers Might Be Able to Cash In on a $20.5 Million Settlement
snippet: The pharmacy chain denies wrongdoing, but is settling anyway.
fullText:
Popular pharmacy chain CVS has been hit with a lawsuit that alleges the company sold data from customers who shopped on its websites (cvs.com and cvshealth.com) or the mobile app. 

The lawsuit alleges that CVS disclosed private health information, browsing data and more from users to advertising company Criteo and other third parties, though the pharmacy denies any wrongdoing. It has settled to the tune of $20.5 million to avoid additional expenses by continuing the lawsuit and other business disruptions. 

Email notifications (PDF) for potential class members were sent out earlier in September, but the deadline to submit the claim form is Nov. 16, 2026. If you’ve ever shopped on any of the CVS websites or mobile apps prior to July 27, 2026, you’re considered eligible to receive payment, but you must still submit a claim. 

			

More from CNET

According to the official settlement website, customers who submit a claim without documentation may receive up to $5, and those who submit a claim with valid documentation of belonging to the class may receive up to $10, but the amount may be reduced depending on the number of valid claims submitted. 

As is typical with class action lawsuits, potential class members may also opt out of the settlement. Opting out of the settlement will prevent payment, but will allow you to maintain your rights to directly sue the company yourself. The final date to opt out of the settlement is Nov. 1, 2026.

The final hearing is set to take place on Dec. 1, 2026, and if the court approves the settlement, payments will be issued 120 days after approval. Class members can be paid via check, PayPal, Venmo or Zelle.

fullText:
Talking to ChatGPT is getting better in three ways starting today. OpenAI is rolling out a collection of improvements to how ChatGPT Voice mode works. 

GPT-6, ChatGPT Work, and plugins

First, ChatGPT Voice can now be powered by OpenAI’s three GPT-6 models. Astra, the most capable, has been out for a few weeks. Sol and Luna, the new medium and small intelligence models were upgraded to GPT-6 yesterday.

Next, OpenAI says that plugins now work with ChatGPT Voice. This includes integration like email, calendar, and Slack. This was a big disconnect for ChatGPT Voice users before, so it should be a highly welcome change.

Lastly, ChatGPT Voice now works with ChatGPT Work on the web and mobile. ChatGPT Work is OpenAI’s cloud-connected agentic system that works everywhere. It’s sort of like Codex on the desktop, but available in more places.

Back in July, OpenAI brought modern voice control to the ChatGPT desktop app. It’s great to see this focus on voice continue with today’s ChatGPT Voice-focused update.

fullText:
Terrence O'Brien

 

is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

Haptics tech company Taction sued Apple in 2021, alleging it infringed two of its patents. Now a federal jury in San Diego has awarded Taction over $5.7 billion in damages. According to CNBC, “The lawsuit centered around U.S. Patent Nos. 10,659,885 and 10,820,117, which both involve vibration-based, tactile transducer technology that helps users feel a device responding to their input.”

Taction argued that Apple’s Taptic Engine in its Apple Watches and iPhones used technology that it had developed without a proper license, and the jury agreed. It found that Apple had infringed on two claims in one patent and one in the other. However, the jury did not find that Apple willfully infringed. Taction had accused Apple of reverse-engineering the tech from two Kannon gaming headsets.

Apple has said that it intends to appeal the decision. We’ve reached out for additional comment and will update the story if and when we hear back.

title: AT&T seemingly has no plans to support Apple’s new iPhone Handoff feature
snippet: Apple last week launched a new iPhone Handoff feature, which lets you use a single phone number across two iPhones. The number intelligently moves between each iPhone based on whichever one you pick up. iPhone Handoff requires support from cellular carriers, and it sounds like AT&T isn’t interested in adopting the feature. more…
fullText:
Apple last week launched a new iPhone Handoff feature, which lets you use a single phone number across two iPhones. The number intelligently moves between each iPhone based on whichever one you pick up.

iPhone Handoff requires support from cellular carriers, and it sounds like AT&T isn’t interested in adopting the feature.

Will AT&T support iPhone Handoff? 

As reported by CNET, AT&T seemingly has no plans to support iPhone Handoff. According to the report:

“While we see that there could be potential in capabilities like iPhone Handoff,” the spokesperson replied, “our focus remains on delivering innovations that make life simpler and keep customers connected with confidence.” They then pointed to “existing eSIM activation and transfer options across compatible devices.”

This will be frustrating news for AT&T subscribers. The carrier’s emphasis on “existing eSIM activation and transfer options” seemingly indicates it doesn’t have a complete grasp on how iPhone Handoff works, and why it’s significantly more seamless than manually moving an eSIM back and forth between two iPhone models.

I’ve been using iPhone Handoff for the last week while testing the iPhone 18 Pro lineup, and it really does feel like magic. As Apple promised, my number instantly switches to whichever iPhone I pick up.

It is a bummer that T-Mobile is charging $5 per month for iPhone Handoff, though it’s not necessarily surprising. It’s still significantly cheaper than having a second cellular plan altogether.

As of right now, T-Mobile is the only carrier in the United States to support iPhone Handoff. Apple says that Verizon will add support by the end of the year, “with more carriers to follow.” Outside the United States, Telekom Germany is a launch partner for the feature. Apple says EE will add support by the end of the year.

title: Apple working on Whoop-style screenless fitness tracker, per report
snippet: Apple is developing a screenless health and fitness tracker to compete with Whoop, according to a new report from Bloomberg. The company is reportedly “developing prototypes,” but has yet to decide whether to ultimately release the product. more…
fullText:
Apple is developing a screenless health and fitness tracker to compete with Whoop, according to a new report from Bloomberg. The company is reportedly “developing prototypes,” but has yet to decide whether to ultimately release the product.

The prototypes being developed inside Apple reportedly have a “thin fabric band with a sensor-equipped computing module.” The project is currently in the “technology investigation” phase, and Bloomberg says the product won’t be released before 2028 — if Apple decides to release it at all.

The project is said to have support from top Apple executives, including Eddy Cue and Tim Cook. Cue took charge of Apple’s health team last October, following the departure of Jeff Williams.

Cue has pushed Apple’s health team to adopt features from the newer rivals, whose products offer simpler interfaces focused squarely on fitness and health tracking. The Apple Watch serves a broader range of purposes.

Products like Whoop and Oura Ring are popular among people who want to track their health and fitness without wearing a smartwatch. As Reuters reports, Oura is prepping for an IPO and recently revealed that it sold 3.6 million Oura Rings in the 12 months ending June 30. Revenue grew 74% to $1.21 billion for the nine months ending June 30.

Apple is still the dominant player in the smartwatch market specifically, though. The Apple Watch also offers a far wider array of features than health and fitness-focused wearables like Oura and Whoop.

Bloomberg also reiterates that next year will be a big year for the Apple Watch:

The company is also working on a major update to its smartwatch lineup for release as early as late 2027. This redesign would follow years of more incremental changes. Apple made its main watch thinner with the Series 10 two years ago, but the larger Ultra model has retained the same look since its debut four years ago.

title: Apple says software update to fix iPhone 18 Pro rebooting bug is coming next week
snippet: On Monday, we reported on an issue where iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max users were seeing their phone freeze and reboot following a failed Face ID attempt. To us, it appeared to be a software glitch rather than an inherent hardware fault. Apple has now confirmed to 9to5Mac that a software update to address this problem is in the works, and should be available early next week. more…
fullText:
On Monday, we reported on an issue where iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max users were seeing their phone freeze and reboot following a failed Face ID attempt. To us, it appeared to be a software glitch rather than an inherent hardware fault.

Apple has now confirmed to 9to5Mac that a software update to address this problem is in the works, and should be available early next week.

Although the bug did not seemingly affect all users, it was reasonably widespread based on social media and 9to5Mac reader reports. 

At the time, we reproduced the problem on an iPhone 18 Pro device by obscuring our face with our hand as we attempted a Face ID authentication to access the Passwords app. The phone simply stops responding to touch input, and hard reboots after a few seconds. You could then find a panic log in the iPhone Analytics section of the Settings app.

iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max feature a redesigned Face ID sensor system, where the Infrared camera has moved behind the under the screen near where the clock is rendered in the status bar, resulting in a 25% smaller visible Dynamic Island. 

As we reported earlier in the week, some customers had already attempted to resolve the rebooting problem by swapping their phone with a new device at Apple, thinking it was a hardware fault. To reiterate, this is not necessary with a software fix now confirmed to be on the way. 

On a somewhat related note, Apple also just released watchOS 27.0.1 to fix a random restart issue with Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4.

title: Astra and Opus just passed Turing’s other test
snippet: Frontier AI models are finishing Alan Turing's World War II codebreaking work.
fullText:
Computer pioneer Alan Turing is best known for his eponymous experiment to test whether artificial and human intelligence can be distinguished. However, the more important test he faced during his lifetime was cracking the Enigma code used by Nazi Germany during World War II.

Now, a pair of cryptanalysts say they’ve cracked two long-unsolved messages encoded by Enigma machines using LLMs built by OpenAI and Anthropic.

While Turing and his team of cryptanalysts built an early computer, dubbed the Bombe, that allowed the United Kingdom to translate Enigma messages during the war, a handful of archival messages remain unbroken — usually due to mistranscription or errors by the original encoders.

Carter Leffen, a developer, simply told OpenAI’s newest model, Astra, to search a database of Enigma messages for an unbroken message and decode it. The model was able to do just that, after doing its own archival research, finding context clues, building a simulator of the Enigma machine, and ultimately recovering the plaintext of a message that had baffled researchers since 2005. He even used Astra to build an interactive website explaining the whole problem.

Frode Weierud, a retired electrical engineer with a lifelong interest in cryptology, maintains the website Crypto Cellar, which includes a variety of resources and records and a database of messages. Last week, Weierud validated Leffen’s solution, which he said left him in “awe.”

Notably, given the lengths that AI agents will go to answer the questions in front of them, the Astra model’s logs include discussion of archived messages in a “private collection” that aren’t hosted by Weierud. He still isn’t sure if the model accessed them or not, but speculates they may have been shared by a different researcher somewhere online, or that the model was able to access the German government’s public archives.

“GPT–6 Astra is behaving like a very professional cryptanalyst and archive researcher,” he wrote. “What it has achieved in two days would take a human researcher weeks or even months. Personally, I spent several weeks researching the Bundesarchiv files GPT–6 Astra refers to.”

On September 21, another cryptanalyst, Jack Willis, a cybersecurity executive, reached out to Weierud, saying he had used Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5 model to break a different unsolved message. Willis provided significantly more guidance to Claude, which was ultimately able to use the known signature of a particular officer’s name to break the message.

Weierud notes that there are just seven unbroken Enigma messages remaining, along with one message where the plaintext is known but the code is still unbroken.

Perhaps not for long.

title: Apple and Qualcomm renew global patent licensing agreement
snippet: Qualcomm and Apple have renewed their global patent licensing agreement, extending a deal that was previously set to expire in 2027. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Qualcomm and Apple have renewed their global patent licensing agreement, extending a deal that was previously set to expire in 2027. Here are the details.

Renewed deal takes effect next year

To say that Apple and Qualcomm have had a rocky relationship would be an understatement.

Once major business partners, the companies became embroiled in a sprawling legal battle in 2017 over Qualcomm’s patent licensing practices and royalty payments.

In a nutshell, Apple sued Qualcomm in U.S. federal court in early 2017, challenging Qualcomm’s patent-licensing practices and seeking nearly $1 billion in royalty rebates that Apple said Qualcomm had improperly withheld.

The lawsuit came just three days after the FTC also sued Qualcomm, alleging anticompetitive licensing practices. The complaint specifically mentioned Qualcomm’s dealings with Apple, alleging that the company offered billions of dollars in conditional rebates in exchange for Apple exclusively using Qualcomm modem chips in new iPhones and iPads.

A few months later, Qualcomm countersued Apple, accusing the company of breaching agreements and interfering with its relationships with iPhone and iPad manufacturers.

The dispute ended in 2019, when Apple and Qualcomm agreed to drop all litigation against each other worldwide.

As part of the settlement, Apple made an undisclosed payment to Qualcomm that, among other things, resolved a dispute over royalty payments Apple had withheld during the legal battle. The companies also entered into a six-year global patent licensing agreement and a separate multiyear chipset supply deal.

That licensing agreement took effect on April 1, 2019, and included an option for Apple to extend it for another two years. Apple ultimately exercised that option, extending the agreement through March 2027.

Today, Qualcomm announced that the companies have renewed the agreement once again, with the new deal taking effect on April 1, 2027.

The full press release read:

Qualcomm Incorporated today announced the renewal of its global patent license agreement with Apple, effective April 1, 2027.

“We are pleased to extend the Apple license agreement,” said John Han, Executive Vice President and General Manager of Qualcomm Technology Licensing (QTL).

The company did not disclose how long the renewed agreement will remain in effect, while Apple has yet to comment on the renewal.

It is worth noting that today’s announcement is unrelated to Apple’s use of Qualcomm modems on iPhones, something that has been widely discussed recently, as Apple used a Qualcomm modem in the U.S. version of the iPhone 18 Pro Max while relying on its own C2 modem elsewhere.

Apple has not officially commented on what its modem plans will look like going forward, but the expectation has been that the company will eventually move away from Qualcomm modems altogether.

title: Apple Podcasts will soon let creators offer exclusive videos to subscribers
snippet: Apple announced this week that creators will soon be able to offer video through Apple Podcasts Subscriptions, “including subscriber-exclusive episodes, ad-free video, early access, and bonus content.” Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple announced this week that creators will soon be able to offer video through Apple Podcasts Subscriptions, “including subscriber-exclusive episodes, ad-free video, early access, and bonus content.” Here are the details.

Apple Podcasts Subscriptions to get support for video

Back in 2021, Apple announced Apple Podcasts Subscriptions. This service lets creators offer paid subscriptions to their shows in exchange for perks such as ad-free listening, bonus episodes, early access, and subscriber-only content.

Since then, creators have been able to offer paid subscriptions through Apple Podcasts to listeners in more than 170 countries and regions.

With the podcast market increasingly shifting toward video, Apple has been expanding the format across its platform.

Earlier this year, Apple introduced a new HLS-based video podcast experience that lets users seamlessly switch between watching and listening, view episodes full-screen, download videos for offline viewing, and more.

More recently, with iOS 27 and its other software updates, Apple expanded video support in Apple Podcasts with features including read-along transcripts, chapters, media links, and playback on Mac and Apple TV.

Now, Apple has announced that video is coming to Apple Podcasts Subscriptions as well.

This means creators will be able to offer subscriber-exclusive video episodes, ad-free video, early access, and bonus video content through the same subscription system currently used for premium audio.

From Apple’s announcement:

Since Apple Podcasts Subscriptions launched, creators have built direct-to-listener businesses around premium audio. Adding video opens new opportunities for you to connect with your audiences and grow your business.

A new way to grow your business: Apple Podcasts Subscriptions already help creators build direct-to-listener businesses around premium audio. With the introduction of video, you have new ways to connect with audiences and expand your business directly on Apple Podcasts.

Streamlined delivery: Deliver both audio and video seamlessly without maintaining separate offerings or workflows.

A familiar Apple experience: Audiences can discover and enjoy premium video across Apple devices and the web, wherever and however they choose to tune in.

Apple says it is currently working with hosting providers to make this integration seamless and will share more details “in the coming months.”

title: Google Maps update shows traffic lights and stop signs at your next turn on Android Auto, more
snippet: Google Maps is rolling out a new update on Android Auto that makes it easier to know what to expect at your next turn, with a visual indicator to show upcoming traffic lights or stop signs. more…
fullText:
Google Maps is rolling out a new update on Android Auto that makes it easier to know what to expect at your next turn, with a visual indicator to show upcoming traffic lights or stop signs.

It’s been around six years since Google Maps started showing traffic lights and stop signs along your route, but a new tweak gives these more relevance to your actual route. Where Maps previously showed these as fixed parts of the map, there’s a new pop-up that shows what to expect at upcoming intersections.

Alongside the floating name of the street at your next turn, Google Maps on Android Auto now also highlights whether you’ll see a traffic light or a stop sign at that intersection. We first observed this behavior earlier this week, and it’s been showing consistently in the time since. It’s also showing on the phone directly, which means iPhone users seeing the update will likely also see this on CarPlay.

It’s a subtle tweak, but it’s also a very glanceable way to give drivers a better idea of what to expect at a coming intersection, which could be invaluable if you’re driving around an unfamiliar area.

	

Like many visual updates, this is likely a server-side update for Google Maps. Let us know in the comments below if you’re seeing this update.

title: Google combines Material 3 Expressive & Liquid Glass on the iPhone [Gallery]
snippet: With Liquid Glass now a year old, Google apps on iOS are beginning to incorporate the translucent material alongside its Material 3 Expressive design language. more…
fullText:
With Liquid Glass now a year old, Google apps on iOS are beginning to incorporate the translucent material alongside its Material 3 Expressive design language.

Previously, the Google Photos floating bottom bar on iOS had a solid background, just like the Android version. As of version 7.94, it’s now made of Liquid Glass.

The screenshots on the left show the “Default” translucency level, while the “More clear” option is on the right and lets you see more of the image behind it. With the dark theme, you see how the default blue accent color tints the current tab indicator.

Google has also updated buttons in the top bar with Liquid Glass.

	

The traditional bottom bar in Google Health has also been updated with Liquid Glass. You can see what’s under the navigation element, while the “Ask Coach” FAB (floating action button) gets a frosted treatment.

The company is still in the process of phasing out the previous Google Material Theme design language on iOS with Material 3. Google Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Keep have been stragglers, while Tasks was updated fairly recently.

More broadly, Google has shown no interest in adding Dynamic Color to its iOS apps. It could add a manual system that lets users choose an accent color across all Google apps. That said, without system access to the wallpaper, it’s a bit pointless, with Dynamic Color always more of a system-level Android feature.

title: Automattic has a new board after failed attempt to put CEO on leave
snippet: After days of upheaval at Automattic, following a failed attempt to remove CEO Matt Mullenweg, the company has a new board.
fullText:
Automattic CEO Matt Mullenweg has rebuilt the company’s board just weeks after its previous directors tried, and failed, to oust him. The board, which was announced to staff Friday, is an eclectic group that includes a best-selling science-fiction author and two co-founders of the now-defunct social app IRL, TechCrunch has learned, and Mullenweg has confirmed.

The new board is the latest twist in an internal governance fight at Automattic, the parent company of WordPress.com, Tumblr, WooCommerce, and others. Earlier this month, the previous board voted to place Mullenweg on leave in an attempt to remove him from the board, only to have the CEO retake control just 33 hours later and remove or accept the resignations of the directors who were involved.

This week, Mullenweg posted about a board meeting but didn’t share who he was meeting with. Now he’s finally informing Automattic employees of the board changes via the company’s announcements channel in Slack.

Sources told TechCrunch the new Automattic board includes: 

American writer Hugh Howey, author of the “Silo” book series. (Mullenweg and Howey both hiked along the Camino de Santiago in Spain back in 2018.)

“Breakup Bootcamp” author Amy Chan (who recently reposted Mullenweg’s tweet about the company’s AI site builder, Spacefast).

IRL co-founder Henry Khachatryan, who Mullenweg described as a “founder and builder,” a longtime collaborator with the late technology writer Om Malik, and the website builder of journalist Nick Bilton.

And Krutal Desai, who co-founded the social app IRL with Khachatryan.

We should note that IRL shut down after investigations revealed that nearly all of its user base was made up of bots. The co-founders, who also included CEO Abraham Shafi, later sued SoftBank and other investors after SoftBank had sued for securities fraud.

New advisers have also joined Automattic, including former Whoop CTO Jaime Waydo, June co-founder Matt Van Horn, and KISSmetrics co-founder Hiten Shah.

In the announcement to staff, Mullenweg reportedly wrote that, “for purposes of Delaware law, I am the CEO, President, Treasurer, and Secretary,” adding that the attempted firing had also brought in “many amazing supporters.”

“We had the most interesting board meeting in a decade (since the Woo acquisition),” he said. 

Reached for comment, Automattic said it hoped to have a comment for TechCrunch soon. After publication, Mullenweg confirmed the board additions and advisors, and shared the following statement: “We are living through times of unprecedented change, possibly a singularity. The next six months will determine the next 20 years of Automattic.” 

Image Credits:Kimberly White/Getty Images for TechCrunch

Automattic’s original board had voted to put Mullenweg on paid leave, but he took back control of the company, letting go of those involved in what he described on X as a “coup attempt.”

To replace the board, Mullenweg leveraged his voting shares — he controls 84% of the vote, he said at TechCrunch Disrupt 2024. The period between his departure and return lasted exactly “33 hours and 20 minutes,” Automattic told TechCrunch previously.

Following the failed board vote, member Toni Schneider, a founding CEO of Automattic and now CEO of Bluesky, resigned from his board position. Mullenweg himself removed General Ann Dunwoody from the board, and board member Sue Decker also resigned. In addition, Mullenweg let go of Automattic CFO Mark Davies, who was slated to become interim CEO, and chief legal officer Andy Missan, TechCrunch confirmed with sources.

Founder advice: If you don't have a coup attempt every few years, you're not hiring strong enough leaders.

— Matt Mullenweg (@photomatt) September 11, 2026

The board never publicly shared its reasons for trying to oust Mullenweg.

Of note, Mullenweg also replaced Automattic’s legal counsel after his return, a move that raises questions about whether the boardroom fight is tied to the company’s ongoing lawsuit with hosting provider WP Engine over trademark disputes and claims over WP Engine’s lack of contribution to the WordPress open source project. (WP Engine’s legal team had also accused Mullenweg this July of destroying evidence, court filings show.)

In an internal message shared after the ousting and return, Mullenweg had acknowledged the chaos it caused, saying:

Last week, several board members formed a special committee and voted to place me on a leave of absence. They did this without advance warning and without giving me a meaningful opportunity to understand or respond to their concerns before they acted. I was denied even a brief extension to consult with independent legal counsel.

I took the steps necessary to reverse that action. I am back and fully in charge of the company. I am again working alongside you to make our company a success.

I also want to share that we have retained Susman Godfrey LLP as our new litigation counsel. Susman Godfrey is one of the top trial firms in the country, and they will be protecting our company’s interests and defending us in our ongoing litigation.

I know this past week has been unsettling. I appreciate your patience and your continued focus on the work that matters. I will have more to share soon, but for now, know that Automattic’s mission and priorities remain unchanged.

Corrections and updates: After publication, TechCrunch updated to clarify that Waydo is the former Whoop CTO. We also added Mullenweg’s statement and confirmation.

title: Disney+ and Hulu just increased prices, here’s how much
snippet: Disney+ and Hulu have just rolled out price increases for most subscription plans, here are the details on new pricing. more…
fullText:
Disney+ and Hulu have just rolled out price increases for most subscription plans, here are the details on new pricing.

Disney has raised prices again on most Disney+ and Hulu streaming plans. The biggest increases hit the ad-free “Premium” plans.

Here’s the new pricing for ad-free plans, effective immediately:

Disney+ Premium (no ads): $21.49/month

Hulu+ Premium (no ads): $21.49/month

Disney+/Hulu Premium Bundle: $21.99/month

These are increases of about two dollars per month compared to the old pricing. Disney+ and Hulu Premium each formerly cost $18.99/month, and the bundle was $19.99. 

Ad-supported plans aren’t exempt from today’s increases. They’re just not getting hit as hard.

Here’s the new pricing for ad-supported plans:

Disney+ (with ads): $12.49/month

Hulu (with ads): $12.49/month

	

Previously, Disney+ and Hulu cost $11.99 each, so the increase is only $.50/month. The bundle pricing for Disney+ and Hulu (with ads) remains $12.99/month as before.

In all these cases, Disney is clearly pushing users to the Disney+/Hulu bundle more than ever. By making it only $.50 more expensive than each standalone service, it’s hard to justify only subscribing to one service.

title: You Might See Prime as a Shipping Option on Sites Other Than Amazon. How It Works
snippet: Some independent stores are now offering Prime delivery without you having to log in to your Amazon account.
fullText:
Free and fast delivery could be an option where you least expect it. More independent stores might be offering Amazon Prime shipping on their websites, and you won’t need to log into your Amazon account to get it.

The announcement this week is an expansion of the company’s Amazon Supply Chain Services, in which merchants pay the company to house their inventory and pick, pack and ship items to customers. Sellers will not have to pay extra to use Prime shipping as an option for customers and can keep their usual payment processing, order management and store policies.

So, imagine you’re shopping for items at one of the thousands of independent, non-Amazon.com stores on the internet. You select some things to buy, head to checkout and see Prime as one of the shipping options. That could mean fast and free, if you have a Prime account.

			

More from CNET

It’s not an entirely new thing — independent stores have offered Prime shipping on their websites before. What’s different now is that you won’t have to click on a “Buy with Prime” widget and then log in to your Prime account. You can finish checkout on the store’s website.

Read more: Amazon’s Early Prime Day Deals Are Here. Grab the Top Discounts Before They’re Gone

If you choose Prime as the shipping option, Amazon will confirm that you’re a member after the order is placed.

CNET reached out to Amazon to see if the company has a list of independent retailers offering Prime shipping, but a representative did not immediately respond.

There are more than 240 million Prime subscribers worldwide, 180 million of those in the US.

title: Apple’s 20th Anniversary iPhone 20 Pro May Arrive as a Seamless Slab of Glass
snippet: Next year’s models could have the biggest screens in iPhone history.
fullText:
Hope there’s extra room in your pockets. A new rumor says Apple’s iPhone 20 Pro and Pro Max could have the largest displays in iPhone history, alongside a quad-curved, nearly all-glass exterior.

Digital Chat Station, a prominent anonymous tech insider on the Chinese social media platform Weibo and a reliable source of Apple news in the past, posted over the weekend that the iPhone 20 Pro screen would be 6.41 inches and the Pro Max 6.96 inches, measured diagonally. The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, which hit stores last Friday, measure 6.27 inches and 6.86 inches (which Apple rounds up to 6.3 inches and 6.9 inches). The iPhone Duo, Apple’s long-awaited first foldable phone, which reaches stores on Oct. 23, has a diagonal 7.6-inch inner display when open.

A representative for Apple did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

			

More from CNET

CNET Senior Reporter Abrar Al-Heeti said that larger screens are great for watching videos and working on the go, but bigger displays also mean higher costs for consumers, serving as an “excuse for companies to charge you more.” 

“Along with the commemorative angle of the iPhone’s 20th anniversary, it’s likely Apple could use design elements like a bigger screen and an all-glass design to hike prices,” Al-Heeti said. 

More glass, smaller Dynamic Island

Digital Chat Station backed Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman’s August report that the exterior of the new flagship phones would be nearly all glass in what’s called a quad-curved design. That means the glass will wrap around all four sides of the phone, making it look as if there is no bezel.

In his report last month, Gurman said that the glass on the front and back of the phones would “curve into the sides of the devices, with a metal band in the middle.”

The exteriors of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are made of aluminum and ceramic glass.

The iPhone 20 Pro and Pro Max will also have a smaller Dynamic Island and a tiny punch-hole selfie cutout on the front, according to Digital Chat Station.

The Dynamic Island is the capsule-shaped region at the top of the front screen that houses the selfie camera. It also expands and contracts to display notifications, system alerts and background activities.

The iPhone 20 Pro and Pro Max are expected to launch in September 2027 as the next iteration in the series. Apple is widely expected to skip over the iPhone 19 name and jump straight to iPhone 20 next year, marking the 20th anniversary of the first iPhone launch in 2007.

title: PNOE’s new face mask wants to make lab-grade breath testing a self-serve affair
snippet: PNOĒ, the Malden, Mass.-based startup whose breath-analyzing mask used to bear an unfortunate resemblance to Bane's, is launching a sleeker self-serve version on October 1 that lets gym-goers measure their VO₂ max and other metabolic markers in eight minutes without a trained operator.
fullText:
At first glance, the newest device from PNOĒ looks like something a comic-book villain might wear. The mask, which covers the nose and mouth and straps around the back of the head, bears more than a passing resemblance to the one worn by Bane, Batman’s hulking nemesis. But its purpose is far more benign; it measures how much oxygen you consume and how much carbon dioxide you exhale, then turns that data into advice about how to eat, train, and, the company hopes, live longer.

PNOĒ, which is based in Malden, Massachusetts, and has operations in Athens, Greece, is preparing to launch the PNOĒ 2.0 on October 1. The big change from its current device is that users can administer the test themselves. According to co-founder and CEO Apostolos Atsalakis, someone can walk into a gym, “just wear the mask, push the button, sit down,” and breathe for eight minutes. “That’s it. It’s that easy,” he said recently, talking with this editor over a Zoom call from the company’s Athens location.

That matters because PNOĒ’s current device requires a trained operator, which limits where it can be used. A self-serve version could open the door to fitness centers without dedicated staff and potentially even pharmacies, Atsalakis said.

The science behind PNOĒ isn’t new. Metabolic testing, which analyzes the gases in a person’s breath to gauge how their body produces energy, has been around for more than a century. For decades, it has been the gold standard for measuring VO₂ max, the maximum amount of oxygen the body can use during exercise and a widely used measure of cardiorespiratory fitness. But the tests have traditionally required bulky, expensive equipment found mainly in sports labs and hospitals, which is why they’ve largely been the province of elite athletes and executive wellness programs.

What 10-year-old PNOĒ promises is the same accuracy in a portable package, paired with software that translates the results into recommendations. “We made it accessible to everyone,” Atsalakis said.

The company says its test captures 23 biomarkers, including (beyond measuring VO₂ max) one’s resting metabolic rate (how many calories the body burns at rest), and metabolic flexibility (how well the body switches between burning fat and carbohydrates). Atsalakis argues that these metrics answer questions that blood tests can’t, such as how many calories a person needs or how they should train.

The timing is good for PNOĒ. VO₂ max has become a buzzword among longevity enthusiasts, thanks in part to research linking higher cardiorespiratory fitness to lower mortality. Atsalakis calls VO₂ max the strongest predictor of human longevity, and he sees his company’s data as a kind of scorecard for the booming wellness industry.

The new device is smaller and more compact than its predecessor, with fewer parts, which Atsalakis said makes it more reliable. It was designed with Milan-based Design Group Italia over what Atsalakis described as “a lot, a lot, a lot of iterations,” since a self-administered metabolic testing device hadn’t been done before.

It also addresses a question that post-pandemic users are likely to ask: who wore it last? The answer: it doesn’t matter, as the electronics detach from the silicone mask and straps, so multiple people can share the costly hardware while each user keeps their own mask.

For all its clinical ambitions, PNOĒ is careful about what it claims. The device isn’t cleared by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, and Atsalakis said that “we do not provide medical recommendations.” Instead, PNOĒ considers itself a wellness device. “It’s like a body composition device, like a scale,” he said. “A doctor cannot prescribe medication based on our results.”

That could change down the road. Researchers have long explored whether compounds in human breath can signal diseases such as cancer, and Atsalakis believes the company’s growing trove of data could eventually help it flag health issues. But he acknowledged that full diagnoses are “definitely a couple of years away,” with regulatory hurdles likely stretching that timeline further. “We’re not there yet,” he said.

PNOĒ traces its roots to Atsalakis’s PhD work in sensing technologies at the University of Cambridge, when wearables were taking off and he became fascinated by what the breath could reveal about the body. He co-founded the company with Panos Papadiamantis, a childhood friend who is now the company’s chief product officer.

The startup went through Y Combinator’s Winter 2019 batch, back when “longevity” was not yet the industry it is today. It has since raised about $22 million, including a recently closed $11 million round, from investors including 50 Years and Google Maps co-founder Lars Rasmussen, who is himself now based in Athens.

PNOĒ sells only to businesses, which then offer the test to their customers. Its clients include Equinox, where it’s available at almost all clubs, said Atsalakis, as well as Four Seasons hotels, Red Bull, the NBA, the Mount Sinai Health System, and the med spa chain Restore Hyper Wellness. 

About 85% of its business comes from the U.S., which Atsalakis described as “by far the most advanced market globally” for longevity. The company is now expanding in Europe and, through partners, in Latin America and Asia.

Businesses pay a subscription ranging from $400 a month to more than $1,000, which covers the hardware, software, training, and marketing materials, a package Atsalakis calls a “business in a box.” PNOĒ also links its results to the services a business sells, so a gym or spa can recommend specific offerings based on a customer’s test. Many clients use the test during onboarding, Atsalakis said, positioning it somewhere between a full clinical workup and the estimates people get from their smartwatches.

That middle ground is increasingly crowded. Apple, Garmin, and Whoop all estimate VO₂ max from heart-rate data, while consumer devices like Lumen analyze breath to gauge fat and carb burning. At the high end, traditional metabolic carts remain the standard in labs and hospitals.

PNOĒ, which employs 110 people, says it recently turned profitable, while growing more than 100% a year. Atsalakis said the company plans to raise a Series B within the next six to 12 months as it tries to put its mask — Bane comparisons and all — in front of more faces.

excerpt:
At first glance, the newest device from PNOĒ looks like something a comic-book villain might wear. The mask, which covers the nose and mouth and straps around the back of the head, bears more than a passing resemblance to the one worn by Bane, Batman’s hulking nemesis. But its purpose is far more benign; it measures how much oxygen you consume and how much carbon dioxide you exhale, then turns that data into advice about how to eat, train, and, the company hopes, live longer.

PNOĒ, which is based in Malden, Massachusetts, and has operations in Athens, Greece, is preparing to launch the PNOĒ 2.0 on October 1. The big change from its current device is that users can administer the test themselves. According to co-founder and CEO Apostolos Atsalakis, someone can walk into a gym, “just wear the mask, push the button, sit down,” and breathe for eight minutes. “That’s it. It’s that easy,” he said recently, talking with this editor over a Zoom call from the company’s Athens location.

title: Apple Watch Ultra 4 includes a new watch face bezel option
snippet: Apple Watch Ultra includes a few more ways to customize your watch face than Series models. These include Ultra-only faces, colors and fonts, and a bezel-type complication. Apple Watch Ultra 4 goes even further, adding a new option in the bezel configuration category. more…
fullText:
Apple Watch Ultra includes a few more ways to customize your watch face than Series models. These include Ultra-only faces, colors and fonts, and a bezel-type complication. Apple Watch Ultra 4 goes even further, adding a new option in the bezel configuration category.

Readiness is a new bezel option on Apple Watch Ultra 4

Both Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 introduce the new Readiness app. This uses data like fitness activity, vitals, and sleep score to present you with a Readiness score.

Overnight vitals include heart rate, respiratory rate, wrist temperature, and recovery HRV. Daytime vitals include heart rate and recovery HRV. 

Apple Watch Ultra 4 faces that support displaying bezel information add Readiness as a new watch face configuration. Bezel options now include:

None

Seconds

Depth

Elevation

Training

Readiness

The Readiness bezel option puts your numerical score and description at the bottom of the watch face.

Four bars wrap the edge of the watch face, showing the different readiness score categories, while a dot indicates where your score fits within that category.

Watch faces like Modular Ultra and the new Siri Modular face support displaying the bezel configuration.

If you’re looking for a way to focus on your readiness score, the new bezel configuration is a great way to keep track of the number.

Since readiness can change throughout the day, it may be worth having front-and-center for a lot of users.

Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 are both available now.

title: Square now integrates with Apple Business to improve Maps listings
snippet: Square has announced a new integration with Apple Business that should make Apple Maps better for both businesses and users. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Square has announced a new integration with Apple Business that should make Apple Maps better for both businesses and users. Here are the details.

Square integration lets businesses easily keep Apple Maps listings up to date with accurate info

Have you ever been frustrated to learn that an Apple Maps business listing has outdated info? Maybe the listed hours are inaccurate, or it has an error in the address, phone number, and so on.

Square’s new integration with Apple Business should help. From the announcement:

Square today announced a new integration with Apple that enables Square sellers to connect their locations to Apple Business from their Square Dashboard, so they can seamlessly manage and synchronize key business location information that appears on Apple Maps. Rather than managing multiple channels separately, sellers can now maintain their Apple presence alongside the rest of their business in Square. The integration makes it easier for sellers to ensure Apple users see up-to-date and accurate information across Apple Maps, Siri AI, Apple Wallet and other Apple apps.

Per Square, this integration provides several key benefits to business owners. It lets them:

Manage their brand and add a logo across connected locations, allowing them to enhance and extend their brand presence to Apple Maps place cards, directly from Square Dashboard.

Automatically sync key business details for each connected location, such as hours, address, and phone number, so this information stays up-to-date and accurate across Apple Maps, Siri AI, Apple Wallet, and other Apple apps and services without manual updates.

Turn discovery into engagement across connected locations with action links such as Menu, Order, Pickup, Delivery, Book, or Schedule Appointment, so customers can take action directly from an Apple Maps place card.

The partnership sounds like a clear win for businesses, since so many already rely on Square. But it should result in a better Apple Maps experience for users over time too.

Business owners can learn more about the Square and Apple Business integration at squareup.com/partnerships/applebusiness.

title: These are my favorite iPhone 18 Pro & Pro Max cases so far [Video]
snippet: The new iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max have been out for a week, and they have been amazing devices to use and test. While the actual footprint and visual design remain unchanged, Apple spiced things up with new colors like Glacier, Burgundy, and a true Deep Black version. These colors are a nice new addition to the iPhone lineup, but, of course, the main question I get asked is: What case should I get to protect my new $ 1,200+ device? Luckily, there are already hundreds of case options for the new 18 Pro lineup, and I have been lucky enough to test a bunch. I know cases are purely subjective and a matter of preference, but I figured I would share some of my favorites! more…
fullText:
The new iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max have been out for a week, and they have been amazing devices to use and test. While the actual footprint and visual design remain unchanged, Apple spiced things up with new colors like Glacier, Burgundy, and a true Deep Black version. These colors are a nice new addition to the iPhone lineup, but, of course, the main question I get asked is: What case should I get to protect my new $ 1,200+ device? Luckily, there are already hundreds of case options for the new 18 Pro lineup, and I have been lucky enough to test a bunch. I know cases are purely subjective and a matter of preference, but I figured I would share some of my favorites!

Be sure to check out our hands-on video with all of these cases to see which one would be best for you!

Pitaka Edge case

I have always leaned towards ultra-thin and minimal cases. I like being able to protect my iPhone while still feeling its actual design. If thinness and lightweight cases are what you are into then Pitaka’s Edge cases are the first option I would consider. You get:

Ultra-thin and lightweight aramid fiber construction

Improved camera protection with a raised camera lip and PitaTap camera control cover

Built-in MagSafe magnets for added strength

Precise cutouts for the buttons, speakers, and USB-C port

Available in a ton of different designs

Even at just 20g and 1mm in thickness, this case offers a ton of protection and rigidity. Pitaka’s Edge case is available today on Amazon for $59 and comes in 10+ colors and designs. 

Nomad Sport Case

Nomad’s Sport Case gives you that perfect balance of everyday protection while staying relatively thin and lightweight. I went with the Lunar Gret color to contrast with the Deep Black iPhone, and it looks fantastic. This case brings:

Smooth, soft-touch exterior with a protective construction

Tactile metal buttons with a textured finish

Microfiber interior lining to help protect your iPhone

Raised camera and screen edges for additional protection

Built-in MagSafe compatibility and a dedicated Camera Control cover

If you want a high-quality, no-frills case that keeps your phone protected while still making it look awesome, I would look into the Nomad Sport case. It’s available on Amazon for $55!

Xtremm Inno E-Ink Case

This is easily one of the most unique and fun cases that I have ever reviewed. The Xtremm Inno  puts a color E-Ink display on the rear of the iPhone that is 100% customizable. You can put any image you want on there, like family photos, team logos, anime characters, literally anything. It’s all done via NFC, so the case does not need a battery, power, or Bluetooth, keeping it as thin and light as any other regular case. It feels like magic. 

Customizable color E-Ink display on the back of the case

NFC technology for transferring images from your iPhone

Support for personal photos and AI-generated designs

Raised camera protection and dedicated Camera Control cover

Built-in MagSafe compatibility despite the rear display

We have a whole video on this to show it off. I recommend watching it before purchasing, just to see how cool this looks! It’s available on Amazon for $75 and comes in five different colors for the new iPhone 18 Pro lineup. 

Rokform Crystal Case

Now, if you need something a bit more rugged with added protection but still want to show off that new burgundy iPhone color, then Rokform is a great choice. Not only is it extremely protective, but It Also has Rokform’s proprietary locking system in addition to MagSafe. This makes it even more useful for someone who needs to securely mount their iPhone on a bike, motorcycle, or other devices that require more than just magnets. 

Rugged construction with reinforced corners and raised edges

Transparent back panel that shows off your iPhone’s color

Rokform’s proprietary twist-lock mounting system

Built-in MagSafe compatibility

Full camera plateau protection with a dedicated Camera Control cover

The Rokform Crystal Case is available on Amazon for $69. They also have their own ecosystem of mounts and attachments worth checking out. 

BodyGuardz Weave Case

This is a brand that I had not heard much about until this year. They have been around for a while, but they just released their new Weave line, and I love the design, texture, and multifunctionality of it all. You get:

Textured woven exterior with a comfortable grip

Integrated kickstand 

Speaker channels designed to direct audio forward

Raised edges for screen and camera protection

Built-in MagSafe 

The speaker directional feature is something I had not seen before, and it actually makes a nice difference. Because of how the speaker cutout is designed, it directs the audio right at you rather than to your left or right. Very unique touch! The BodyGuardz Weave is available on Amazon for $59

Andar Aspen

If you are someone who misses the old iPhone leather cases of years past, then Andar is the next best alternative. I have been using their cases for years, and they are some of the best leather cases on the market. You get:

Genuine leather exterior that develops a unique patina over time and smells fantastic 

Soft microfiber interior lining 

Raised edges around the display and camera for additional protection

Dedicated Camera Control cover and tactile metal buttons

Built-in MagSafe compatibility and multiple color options

Their new black color matches the Deep Black iPhone so well that it almost makes the iPhone disappear in the shadows. They have over 10 colors to choose from, and these cases just get better with time. The Andar Aspen Case is available for $70 and can be purchased directly through Andar.

Spigen Nano Pop Case

Spigen’s Nano Pop case is a great option if you are looking for something that will color-match and enhance your new iPhone. It has a two-tone design that looks especially nice with the new Burgundy iPhone, and it also has uniquely textured sides for additional grip in the hand. The Pop case gives you:

Two-tone design with contrasting colors

Flexible, rubberized construction with textured sides for additional grip

Raised edges and protection around the entire camera plateau

Dedicated Camera Control cover

Built-in lanyard attachment point

This one is the most budget-friendly of the bunch as well, sitting at just $21 directly from Amazon

Final take

As I mentioned in the intro, cases are highly subjective purchases. It is almost like clothing but for your phone. There is no right or wrong answer to any of these, just a matter of what you think works and looks best. All of these have their own unique selling points and differentiators, and they come from very reputable brands, so there is no going wrong with any of them. I personally like to keep it as thin and light as possible, while I know my brother likes his cases bulky and protective. 

Be sure to catch our video on these, as we go hands-on with all of these cases, and leave a comment on some other brands I need to check out. I would love to give you guys a round two of my favorite cases later in the year. For those people waiting for the iPhone Duo, we will also have something similar for the new device.
